item.text: I’ll trace the registration and invitation code plus existing tests, write the required checkpoint first, then update the implementation and run the focused existing tests.

item.command: /bin/bash -lc "pwd && rg --files -g 'AGENTS.md' -g '*invite*' -g '*register*' -g 'package.json' -g '*test*' | head -200"
/bin/bash -lc "pwd && rg --files -g 'AGENTS.md' -g '*invite*' -g '*register*' -g 'package.json' -g '*test*' | head -200"

/bin/bash -lc "mkdir -p .codex-role-output && cat > .codex-role-output/checkpoint.md <<'EOF'
# Checkpoint

Task: allow registration with a valid invitation token without requiring email, while preserving invitation confirmation, group membership, inviter references, and complete cleanup.

Initial status: repository inspection started. "'`rg` is unavailable in this environment; using `find` and targeted file reads instead.
EOF
find .. -name AGENTS.md -print; find src -type f | grep -Ei '"'(invite|register|user)' | head -200; find . -maxdepth 3 -name package.json -print"

item.text:
Implemented token-based invitation registration.

- The registration client copies `token` from the URL into the hidden form field.
- Registration with a token skips the email collection interstitial, confirms the email only when it matches the invitation, joins the invited groups, and cleans up invitation records.
- Invitation lookup and metadata now use token keys, with per-email token sets and inviter references. Verification accepts a token without an email; cleanup accepts either a token or email.

ESLint and `git diff --check` passed. The invitation tests could not start because Redis was unavailable at `127.0.0.1:6379`.
